title: ר' אבין

paragraphs: Rabbi Avin was with a king and departed without the customary leave-taking. The king wished to kill him, but saw two fiery sparks issuing from his neck and left him alone. The commentator writes that he saw two tefillin straps, Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, chapter 5, mishnah 1. His father died when his mother became pregnant; his mother died when he was born, Jerusalem Talmud, Kiddushin, chapter 1, halakhah 7. When he died Rabbi Hoshaya of Terya was born. Midrash Kohelet on “Sweet is the laborer’s sleep”: when Rabbi Bon died, etc., what did the king do? He took him by the hand and walked with him, etc. G.N. writes that he is Jeroboam, to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, said, “You and I shall walk in the Garden of Eden.” Rabbi Avin died during the festival, and Rabbi Mana did not perform kindness for him. The people of Sepphoris said, “Hatred until death!” After the festival he honored him, Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Megallechin, halakhah 7. Rabbi Avin’s father recited a teaching: Yoma 29, end of a; Bava Kamma 117a; Niddah 37a; Sanhedrin 76a; Gittin 53a. Rabbi Avin’s father recited before Rabbi Zeira, chapter Hamegaresh 85a. The law follows Ravin rather than Rav Dimi, since Ravin is reliable, as in chapter Haba Al Yevimto (Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 73a).
All these had fathers named Avin.

Abaye; Rabbi Adda; Rabbi Achadvoy—requires examination; Rav Idi; Rav Ika; Rav Ammi; Rav Ashi; Rav Bibi; Rav Dimi; Rav Huna; Rabbi Chiyya; Rabbi Chinena; Rabbi Yehoshua; Rabbi Yochanan—requires examination; Rabbi Yose; Rabbi Yosef; Rabbi Yaakov; Rav Yitzchak; Rav Kohen; Rav Maryon; Rav Natan; Shmuel.

Because the Arukh writes that Ravin is Rabbi Avin in shortened speech, I arranged every Ravin under alef with Avin. Yuchasin separated them, and most are duplicates. I shall arrange Rabbi Avin/Ravin’s teacher, student, colleague, and contemporaries, since they are one.

Rabbi Abba; Abba, Shmuel’s father—requires examination there. In Abba Kohen Bardela’s name; in Rabbi Abbahu’s name, Gittin 9b. He went with Abaye and called Abaye “master,” Berakhot 47, beginning of a. Abaye told him, “Avin the bereaved, should one say such a thing?”, Pesachim 70b; and, “Avin the bereaved, why did you not eat udder?”, Chullin 110a. In Rabbi Acha’s name. He said in Rabbi Ila’s name, Avodah Zarah 51b; Jerusalem Talmud, Ketubbot, chapter 2, halakhah 5; he asked before him, beginning of Demai. He said in Rabbi Ilai’s name: Menachot 36b; Mo'ed Katan 3a; Sotah 5a; Shabbat 5a, two things; Yevamot 48; Bava Batra 171. In Rabbi Elazar’s name: Pesachim 71a; Sukkah 21b; Yevamot 63a. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yose in his name—requires examination there in the amoraic generation. Betiti in his time. In R. Binyamin bar Levi’s name; in R. Berekhiah the elder’s name. Rav Dimi came to the Land of Israel before Ravin. He sat with Rav Huna before Rabbi Yirmeyah. Rav Huna sat before him, Jerusalem Talmud, Bameh Ishah; he objected to Rav Huna. Rav Huna the priest in his name. He asked Ze'ira. Rabbi Chizkiyah. He said in Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba’s name in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Kiddushin 75b. In Rabbi Chiyya’s name, Sanhedrin 63a—perhaps it should read Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba. In Rabbi Chanan bar Abba’s name in Rav’s name, Shabbat 114b. In Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Menachot 71, end of b; Berakhot 47a; Shabbat 5a. In Rabbi Yonatan’s name, Yoma 41, end of b. In Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s name, Shabbat 94b. Ravin sent in Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina’s name, Chullin 101b. In Rabbi Yose’s name in Resh Lakish’s name, Keritot 25b—it seems it should read Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, or Rav Yosef; the new Talmud editions did not correct it. In Rabbi Yannai’s name, chapter Haddar—requires examination. In Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi’s name, end of Rosh Hashanah. Rabbi Yitzchak; Rabbi Yitzchak Sumaka. When he ascended, he said before Rabbi Yirmeyah, “Foolish Babylonians! Because they dwell in a dark land they say dark teachings,” Pesachim 34b; Zevachim 60b; Bekhorot, chapter 3, 25b. He said in Rabbi Yirmeyah’s name; walked behind Rabbi Yirmeyah, Shabbat 108b; sat before Rabbi Yirmeyah, Nedarim 29b. In Rabbi Meir’s name, Bereshit Rabbah, sections 45, 48. Rabbi Meyasha. Maryon, his son. He sat before Rabbana Nechemyah, the exilarch’s brother. He spoke to Rav Amram, Berakhot 49b—it seems it should read Rav Idi bar Avin spoke to Rabbi Amram, since just before it Rav Idi bar Avin speaks in Rabbi Elazar’s name. The new Talmud editions did not correct it. In Rabbi Pinchas’s name, Shekalim, beginning of chapter 7. He said several things in Rav’s name, Nedarim 40a—requires examination; also Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Sheloshah She'akhalu, in Rav’s name. Rava said in Ravin’s name, Shabbat 12b. Rabbi Shammai in Rabbi Acha’s name. Shekalim says Rabbi Shemi; the Jerusalem Talmud there has Rabbi Shammai. In Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak’s name, Shekalim, chapter 3; in R. Shmuel of Cappadocia’s name. In Rabbi Shimon’s name: the Holy One, blessed be He, joined His right hand with Abraham and circumcised him, Shir Hashirim Rabbah; and Midrash Eikhah: the Holy One, blessed be He, will sit as at a threshing floor. In Resh Lakish’s name, Bava Metzia 101a and end of Hasho'el; Pesachim 56b. In Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi’s name, Ketubbot 50a. Rav Tachlifa bar Ma'arava spoke to him. [Glosses: Avin: (a) Me'ilah 9a: Shmuel’s father and Rabbi Avin object to Rav Huna. This requires examination: Ketubbot 51b has Rav objecting to Shmuel’s father, so Rav appears his student, while Rav Huna was Rav’s student. How could Shmuel’s father object to his student’s student? It cannot be Rav Huna the exilarch in Rabbi’s days, since he and Ravin questioned Rav Huna, and Ravin was not in Rabbi’s days: Shabbat 63b has Ravin and Rav Huna sitting before Rabbi Yirmeyah. The new Talmud editions delete ‘and Ravin’; other readings omit ‘to Rav Huna.’ This pleased me. (b) Shabbat 139b: Rav Avin bar Rav Huna should read Avin bar Huna; not corrected. (c) Sanhedrin 63a: Rabbi Avin said in Rabbi Chiyya’s name—I think it should read ‘son of Rabbi Chiyya,’ as the new Talmud editions have it. (d) Berakhot 49b: Rabbi Avin spoke to Rav Amram. It seems it should read Rav Dimi bar Avin, mentioned there speaking in Rabbi Amram’s name; not corrected.]
